headline: High: n8n can write and execute server-side workflows while spring-integration-samples has no documented runtime controls, creating default-risk for data leakage and cascading automation errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can ingest workflow inputs and files via server filesystem and integrations, so prompt-like content could be routed into its AI Agent nodes. spring-integration-samples has no documented runtime ingestion surface or shared channel, so the pairwise injection path is indirect and likely requires manual bridging.
conditions: IF the operator copies spring-integration-samples content into an n8n workflow input or file node, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two, the risk increases.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted text into n8n AI Agent nodes.
Use a separate staging folder for any files passed between agents.
Add a manual review step before n8n executes instructions extracted from B.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to workflow inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n has broad network egress and server filesystem access, so it can transmit workflow data off-box by default. spring-integration-samples is documented with network_egress none, but the pair still creates leakage risk if shared workflow data includes sensitive content processed by n8n and then exposed through integrations.
conditions: IF the workflow processes secrets, customer data, or files in n8n, those contents can flow to external integrations.
IF B is used as a source of files or text for n8n, that content can be exfiltrated by A's integrations.
mitigations: Restrict n8n credentials to least-privilege scopes.
Avoid passing sensitive files from B into n8n.
Turn off unused integration nodes in n8n workflows.
Review outbound destinations before enabling a workflow.
requires-engineering: isolate n8n on a separate network segment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n can write the server filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while spring-integration-samples is a code/sample repository with no write or locking controls documented. If both touch the same workspace or connected system, concurrent writes and state drift are plausible; uncertainty about B's runtime behavior pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or connected datastore, write conflicts can occur.
IF B is deployed as a mutable runtime rather than a static sample repo, overlap risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories to A and B.
Prevent n8n from writing into the repository checkout.
Use file locks or a single-writer policy for shared artifacts.
Review any shared OAuth or API credentials before execution.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n's AI Agent node can orchestrate tools and actions, so if it consumes outputs from spring-integration-samples without verification, errors can cascade into automated side effects. B is only a sample repo, but the pair still supports a default path where A's output becomes actionable input for A's own workflows.
conditions: IF n8n treats text or code from B as authoritative workflow logic, downstream actions may be wrong.
IF a workflow uses A to trigger emails, API calls, or file writes based on B-derived content, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Add a human approval step before any side-effecting node.
Require schema validation on data imported from B.
Log and diff B-derived inputs before execution.
Limit AI Agent nodes to read-only analysis where possible.
requires-engineering: separate planning from execution workflows.

E_compliance.rationale: n8n handles secrets per-credential store and broad workflow data, while spring-integration-samples is an open-source sample repo with no documented residency or retention obligations. The main compliance issue is operational: if regulated data is routed through n8n, its storage and integration behavior may exceed what B documents, but B itself adds no separate residency constraint.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in n8n workflows, retention and access controls must be reviewed.
IF the operator relies on B as a compliance boundary, that assumption is false because B has no documented controls.
mitigations: Inventory regulated data classes before enabling workflows.
Restrict n8n credential access to named operators.
Document retention settings for workflow executions.
Avoid routing PHI or EU PII through undocumented sample workflows.
requires-engineering: add formal data-processing agreements and residency controls.
